Reason: The chest X-ray shows marked elevation of the right hemidiaphragm, which is a classic sign of right diaphragmatic paralysis (often presenting with respiratory symptoms like a persistent cold/cough due to atelectasis or reduced clearance), while the scalloped appearance of the left hemidiaphragm represents normal muscular slips (diaphragmatic eventration/variant) rather than pathology.
